summary: This benchmark evaluates whether transplanting a feed-forward expert from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B into Qwen2.5-14B preserves a matching-bracket log-odds signal across four controlled intervention conditions. The empirical findings establish that passing exact donor outputs through an affine mapping into the 14B receiver fails to recover the signal (-0.009 vs. +2.111 native effect), localizing the failure boundary to the joint affine map and subsequent receiver path. The study is rigorously controlled with precise model revisions, ablation baselines, and bootstrap confidence intervals, although it represents a narrow micro-benchmark on a single model pair.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design isolating input adaptation versus output mapping and receiver downstream dynamics across matched source/destination contrasts.
Comprehensive statistical reporting using paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals across 256 test groups.
Meticulously documented environmental specifications, including exact Hugging Face commit hashes, layer indices, dimensionalities, and MLX runtime versions.
Valuable negative result in the area of cross-model representation surgery and modular grafting.
weaknesses: Narrow empirical scope restricted to a single donor-receiver pair (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B to Qwen2.5-14B) and a single intervention position (block 27/28).
Does not disentangle whether failure stems primarily from the linear expressivity limits of the affine ridge regression map or internal representation mismatch in block 28 and subsequent layers.
Brief exposition that omits broader literature context on model stitching and representation alignment.
suggestions: Conduct a dimensional or rank ablation on the affine mapping (e.g., comparing linear/ridge regression against low-rank non-linear adapters) to isolate the mapping error from receiver integration error.
Test intermediate block readouts (e.g., tuned lens or linear probes immediately after block 28) to measure where the bracket signal attenuates along the receiver path.

The receiver is Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B base revision 97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9.
